messages.subject: is it a poorly shaped delaunay triangulation for spde ?
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to understand how Delaunay traingulation works and I have here a few questions regarding my graph with 5257 vertices:

1. What defines here a boundary of the triangulation? Why are they so far extended? (I guess it relates to the recent discussion on variances at the boundaries?)
2. Are these triangles 'poorly shaped' (some of them are very elongated)?
3. Which algorithm is used for Delaunay triangulation?
Why, for instance at the bottom of the convex hull I have only one point that seems to deform all triangles?


Many thanks,
Olga

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] is it a poorly shaped delaunay triangulation for spde ?
parts:
On 18/02/13 11:31, Olga Lyashevska wrote:
> I am trying to understand how Delaunay traingulation works and I have
> here a few questions regarding my graph with 5257 vertices:

> 1. What defines here a boundary of the triangulation? Why are they so
> far extended? (I guess it relates to the recent discussion on
> variances at the boundaries?)

By default, the domain extended by a certain proportion around an
approximation of the convex hull. In your case, it might make more
sense to specify a non-convex boundary instead, depending on what your
domain represents.
> 2. Are these triangles 'poorly shaped' (some of them are very elongated)?

Yes, the triangles in your figure are very "bad". You appear to have
only asked for a triangulation of your existing points (plus the
automatic boundary), but you must also specify that you want a "refined"
triangulation; see more below.

> 3. Which algorithm is used for Delaunay triangulation?
> Why, for instance at the bottom of the convex hull I have only one
> point that seems to deform all triangles?

Since you did not ask for a refined triangulation, the program gave you
a pure Delaunay triangulation of your existing points. If you instead
ask for a refined triangulation, points will be added iteratively at
strategic locations to improve the shape (and size) of the triangles.
See
http://people.bath.ac.uk/fl353/isba/
for an example using inla.mesh.create.helper()

Finn L
